short_name: CIRCIA (Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act of 2022) - proposed 6 CFR Part 226
citation: 6 U.S.C. 681-681g; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (NPRM 89 FR 23644, Apr. 4, 2024)
summary: Would require covered entities to report covered cyber incidents to CISA within 72 hours and ransom payments within 24 hours, and preserve related data.
applies_to: Entities in a critical infrastructure sector that exceed the SBA small-business size standard for their NAICS code, or meet a sector-based criterion. Sector criterion: owns or has business operations in primary metal (NAICS 331), machinery (333), electrical equipment/appliance/component (335) or transportation equipment (336) manufacturing - regardless of size; also OT hardware/software OEMs under the IT criterion.
size_thresholds: Proposed 226.2(a): exceeds SBA size standard in 13 CFR Part 121 for the entity's NAICS code (employee- or revenue-based depending on NAICS); sector-based criteria apply regardless of size.
status: NOT YET IN EFFECT. NPRM published Apr. 4, 2024; comment period closed Jul. 3, 2024; CISA held additional town halls in 2026 (FR notices Feb. 13, 2026 and May 26, 2026) on scope and burden. Fall 2025 Unified Agenda projected the final rule for 09/2026; no final rule found in the Federal Register as of 2026-09-25. Reporting obligations begin only on the final rule's effective date.

short_name: ICTS Supply Chain: Connected Vehicles rule
citation: 15 CFR Part 791, Subpart D (90 FR 5414, Jan. 16, 2025)
summary: Prohibits connected-vehicle transactions involving VCS hardware or ADS/VCS software designed/supplied by PRC- or Russia-linked persons; requires Declarations of Conformity and supply-chain due diligence.
applies_to: Connected vehicle manufacturers and VCS hardware importers.
size_thresholds: No size threshold; phased by model year - software prohibitions from model year 2027; VCS hardware from model year 2030 (or units imported on/after Jan. 1, 2029).
status: In effect (final rule Jan. 2025) with model-year phase-in.

summary: Controls export, reexport and release (deemed exports) of dual-use items, software and technology; end-to-end encrypted technology/software meeting FIPS 140-2 or equivalent is not an export.
applies_to: Manufacturers and holders of EAR-controlled technology, software and items.

short_name: DFARS 252.204-7012 Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting
summary: Requires 'adequate security' including NIST SP 800-171 on systems with covered defense information (CDI), FedRAMP Moderate-equivalent cloud, 72-hour incident reporting, malware submission, 90-day image preservation, and flowdown.
applies_to: DoD contractors and subcontractors whose performance involves CDI or operationally critical support.
size_thresholds: No small-business exemption; flowdown required to subcontracts involving CDI/operationally critical support, including commercial products/services.
